Border crossings

Customs clearance at the Haj Omran border crossing (Tamarchin)

Last updated: 31 October 2026

Crossing at a glance

The Haj Omran crossing in Erbil Governorate, Kurdistan Region, faces the Tamarchin crossing near Piranshahr in Iran's West Azerbaijan Province. It serves goods coming from Urmia, Tabriz and north-western Iran towards Erbil and the region's cities along a mountain road.

Iraqi side
Haj Omran crossing — Erbil Governorate, Kurdistan Region
Iranian side
Tamarchin — Piranshahr, West Azerbaijan Province
Serves in Iraq
Erbil, Duhok and northern Iraq
Routes from Iran
Urmia, Tabriz, Mahabad and north-western Iran
Our service
Import, export and transit clearance, with follow-up until release
Chat on WhatsApp+964 786 709 4651

When to choose this crossing

  • Your goods are going to Erbil or Duhok.
  • Goods coming from West Azerbaijan and north-western Iran.

Practical notes

  • The crossing is in the Kurdistan Region and run by the regional authorities, so some procedures can differ from crossings in central and southern Iraq.
  • The road is mountainous and can be affected by snow in winter; plan shipping dates early.

How we clear your goods

We review your documents before loading, file the customs declaration when the truck arrives, follow the inspection and duty payment through to release, and update you on WhatsApp at every stage.

Read the Iran–Iraq customs clearance guide

Questions about this crossing

Do you clear goods at the Haj Omran crossing?

Yes. We follow the clearance of shipments entering through Haj Omran to Erbil and the Kurdistan Region, from document review to release.

Are procedures different at Kurdistan Region crossings?

The regional authorities run their own border crossings, so some procedures and requirements can differ from those in central and southern Iraq. We review your shipment in advance and explain what is needed before loading.

Is the Haj Omran crossing affected by the weather?

The road to the crossing is mountainous and can be affected by snow in winter, so we recommend allowing extra time for shipments in that season.
